_comment: The Perfect Dark bodies + clips the game ships, for `pd_gltf.py batch`.
`clip_rig` only supplies bone names and rest offsets. Every chr on the shared 15-bone rig
yields the same names, which is all the engine binds against, so one export drives them all.
A character is `body` or `[body, head]`. Only a51guard, dd_shock and elvis have a head
built in; the other 62 carry a HEADSPOT and need one naming a `head*.bin`. PD mixes heads
and bodies freely (g_HeadsAndBodies), so these pairings are a choice, not a derivation.
TEXTURES: four bodies (a51guard, dd_shock, elvis, testchr) store their textures inline in
the model file; everything else indexes the compressed global pool, decoded by pd_tex.py.
Both paths work, so any of the 65 shared-rig bodies can be exported fully textured. The
handful of pool textures still on PD's non-zlib codec fall back to the debug palette per
affected triangle, which is why the odd small patch may read flat.
_clips_comment: THE HUNTER CLIP SET, in the engine's fixed 36-slot layout. `World::new` builds a
template whose indices the combat code does arithmetic on (`FIRE_*_IDX`,
`CHAR_HIT_START`, `CHAR_HIT_START + HIT_CLIPS.len()`), so the ORDER of the 36 keys
below is load-bearing and the filenames are numbered to make that visible on disk:
00-03  idle / walk / jog / run
04-06  fire: rifle / pistol / dual
07-18  the 12 hit reactions   (parallel to engine `anim_set::HIT_CLIPS`)
19-35  the 17 deaths          (parallel to engine `anim_set::DEATH_CLIPS`)
WHY THESE IDS: Perfect Dark and GoldenEye share one animation bank. Rare carried the
GE character animations into PD at the SAME numbers, so a GE clip named `2A-jogging`
is PD's `ANIM_002A`. That is not an inference from the names — it was measured, and
`pd_animmap.py` re-measures it: 26 of the 36 GE clips the game already ships match a
PD animation of the same id frame-for-frame, and the posed body traces the same
posture curve over the clip (GE's 21-death 1.80 -> 0.34 m, PD's ANIM_DEATH_0021
2.07 -> 0.38 m, matching turn for turn at the 1.15x height ratio).
The exceptions are honest ones. Six GE death clips have no PD counterpart at that id:
PD's ANIM_0016/0018/001B/001D/001E/001F are different animations that never leave
their feet (checked with `pd_triage.py`; they also differ in frame count, two
independent signals agreeing). Those six slots are filled with deaths PD has and
GoldenEye does not, taken from `g_DeathAnimsHuman*` (`game/chraction.c:228+`) and
named for the hit part whose table lists them. The set is more Perfect Dark for it,
not less.
Two ids also disagree about their NAME rather than their content: GE ships
`39-death-left-leg`, which PD's own symbols call ANIM_DEATH_STOMACH_LONG. Same 187
frames, same animation; PD's name is the authored one, so it is used here.
Idle is ANIM_TWO_GUN_HOLD (0x01) and matches GE's `00-idle` at 163 frames — the one
place the two banks are off by one, because PD's slot 0 is a null entry.
The fire clips are the standing attack animations: 0x32 is what GE ships as
`01-fire-standing` (106 frames, both) and is a member of PD's own
g_StandHeavyAttackAnims (`chraction.c:956`).
